correctness.rationale: A strict endomorphism gives a unique signed closed walk. Winding ±1 gives exactly the units; winding zero forces a balanced word and a reversal, hence a repeated image. A commuting rotation of nonzero step k forces period gcd(n,k); the sum per period is zero for a balanced word, contradicting f(i+k)=f(i)+k. A commuting reflection pairs steps by i↦c−1−i and imposes 2f(0)=c−sum_{i=0}^{c−1} ε_i modulo 2m. For c=0 there are m pairs and balance needs m even. For c=1 two fixed steps require paired sum ±1 if m is even, or 0 if m is odd; the initial congruence has two solutions. This reproduces all three parity counts and the unit contribution of four. Two distinct reflections cannot stabilize a singular map, so the reflection incidence sum 2nH_m counts distinct singular maps and gives precisely the two stated orbit sizes. The dihedral unit classes give the remaining terms (including the merged y² coefficient at n=4); Stirling yields both asymptotics. An independent JavaScript enumeration extended vertex-image tuples by adjacent images and retained those whose last image was adjacent to the first. For each actual map and unit it tested f(u(i))=u(f(i)) and formed conjugates via f_u(u(i))=u(f(i)). For n=4,6,8,10,12,14,16 the resulting singular size-(n,2n) orbit counts were (4,1),(4,8),(12,29),(12,120),(40,442),(40,1696),(140,6365), and every unit centralizer agreed. Odd n=5,7,9,11 gave only units and the stated odd orbit histogram. This finite check corroborates the universal proof, not the reverse.

value.rationale: Conjugation identifies relabelings of an endomorphism by a single graph symmetry, a natural equivalence in a unit-bearing monoid. The two-size classification on all singular maps quantifies precisely how often any polygon symmetry persists, with an exact reflection-axis distinction and an exponentially small exceptional proportion. This supplies stabilizer information absent from labeled totals and rank or kernel counts.
